newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REED, GALARRAGA PACE 16-HIT COLORADO ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REED, GALARRAGA PACE 16-HIT COLORADO ATTACK.

text.p: Jeff Reed and Andres Galarraga each had three hits, including a two-run homer apiece, to lead the Colorado Rockies to a 9-6 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday.

Galarraga belted his 17th homer in the first inning and Reed put the Rockies ahead to stay with his two-run shot in the sixth, while Vinny Castilla went 3-for-4 and drove in a run as Colorado erupted for 16 hits against Atlanta pitching.
"I want to play as much as possible. I helped the team today and we came out on top," said Reed, who was 3-for-3.

Chris Brock made his major-league debut for Atlanta and left after four innings with a 4-3 lead. But in the sixth, reliever Brad Clontz (2-1) gave up a single to Castilla before Reed hit a 2-1 pitch over the fence in left-centre.

Colorado padded its lead in the seventh against Mike Bielecki, the fourth of five Braves' pitchers, as Galarraga singled and scored on Castilla's RBI single. Reed then drove home Castilla with an RBI single and scored on Jason Bates's double to make it 8-4.
Colorado starter John Thomson (2-4) picked up the win, giving up four runs and eight hits in 6 2/3 innings.
The Braves, who have lost three of their last four games, got five of their runs on home runs by Fred McGriff, Eduardo Perez and Chipper Jones.
In San Francisco, Bobby Bonilla hit a three-run homer and drove in four runs to lead the Florida Marlins to a 6-3 victory over the Giants.
Bonilla's three-run homer followed an RBI double by Gary Sheffield in the first, staking the Marlins to a 4-0 lead. He added an RBI fielder's choice in the fifth.
Rick Helling (2-4) picked up the win despite walking seven in five innings. He allowed two runs and five hits as the Giants left 15 men stranded on base.

"The way Kevin Brown pitched yesterday, I was the exact opposite today," Helling said, referring to Brown's no-hitter Tuesday. "I didn't throw all that well, but it just goes to show you don't have to pitch great to get a W (win)."
In Los Angeles, Raul Mondesi belted a three-run homer in the first inning and a two-run blast in the seventh to power the Dodgers to a 10-5 victory over the Houston Astros.

Mondesi drove a 2-2 offering from Mike Hampton (2-5) over the left-field wall to stake the Dodgers to a 3-0 first-inning lead. With Los Angeles nursing a 5-4 edge in the seventh, he victimised reliever Ramon Garcia for a two-run shot to centre.
Eric Karros and Mike Piazza also homered for Los Angeles, which scored nine of its 10 runs via homers.
Chan Ho Park (5-3) allowed four runs and five hits in seven innings for the win.
At Chicago, Scott Servais scored the winning run on Greg McMichael's wild pitch in the bottom of the eighth inning as the Cubs edged the New York Mets 5-4 to snap a six-game slide.
Servais led off the eighth with a single, was sacrificed to second by Rey Sanchez and advanced to third on a groundout before McMichael's wild pitch on a 1-2 count.
Terry Adams (1-3) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings with two strikeouts to earn the win. McMichael (3-5) suffered the loss.
In Cincinnati, Brett Tomko allowed one run over seven innings and pinch-hitter Terry Pendleton's RBI double snapped a seventh-inning tie to lead the Reds to a 2-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Tomko (2-1) scattered four hits, walked two and struck out five. Jeff Shaw finished up to notch his 12th save.

Hal Morris singled and Brett Boone doubled off starter Esteban Loaiza (5-3) in the seventh before Joe Oliver's sacrifice fly tied the game. Then with runners at the corners, Pendleton -- batting for Tomko -- lined a double over centre fielder Adrian Brown's head to bring home the winning run.

In Montreal, Mark Grudzielanek snapped an eighth-inning tie with an RBI double and Jim Bullinger pitched eight solid innings as the Expos extended their winning streak to six games with a 4-3 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Grudzielanek's game-winning hit was his major league-leading 24th double of the season.
Bullinger (4-5) allowed three runs and six hits for the win. Phillies reliever Jerry Spradlin (1-3) took the loss.
Ryan McGuire and Mike Lansing homered for Montreal off Phillies starter Matt Beech. McGuire has hit in all seven games since his recall from the minors.

In San Diego, Royce Clayton highlighted a five-run seventh inning with a bases-loaded triple and Dmitri Young collected three hits and three RBI to lead the St Louis Cardinals to an 8-3 victory over the Padres.

Alan Benes (6-5) won for the third time in four starts, allowing three runs and four hits over six innings. He walked four and struck out 11 strikeouts. Mark Petkovsek finished for the Cards, giving up two hits with four more strike outs.
San Diego reliever Terry Burrows (0-2), who came on in the seventh inning, suffered the defeat.
